:::{#exr-bernoulli-hessian-contribution}
#### Hessian contribution of one binary outcome

In the setting of @exr-bernoulli-score-contribution,
derive the [Hessian](#def-hessian) contribution $\hess_\iobs(\prob) \eqdef \deriv{\prob} \score_\iobs(\prob)$ of observation $\iobs$.
Start from the [score](#def-score) contribution written as a difference of two fractions,
$\score_\iobs(\prob) = \outvar_\iobs / \prob - (1 - \outvar_\iobs) / (1 - \prob)$,
the form in @sol-derive-bernoulli-score before its fractions are combined.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-bernoulli-hessian-contribution}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hess_\iobs(\prob)
&= \deriv{\prob} \score_\iobs(\prob)
&& \text{(definition of the Hessian contribution)}\\
&= \deriv{\prob} \paren{\frac{\outvar_\iobs}{\prob} - \frac{1 - \outvar_\iobs}{1 - \prob}}
&& \text{(score contribution as a difference of fractions)}\\
&= \deriv{\prob} \paren{\outvar_\iobs \prob^{-1} - (1 - \outvar_\iobs) (1 - \prob)^{-1}}
&& \text{(write each fraction as a negative power)}\\
&= \outvar_\iobs \deriv{\prob} \prob^{-1} - (1 - \outvar_\iobs) \deriv{\prob} (1 - \prob)^{-1}
&& \text{(linearity and constant multiple rule)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The first derivative is:

$$
\deriv{\prob} \prob^{-1}
= -\prob^{-2}
\qquad \text{(power rule)}
$$

The second derivative needs the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\prob} (1 - \prob)^{-1}
&= -(1 - \prob)^{-2} \deriv{\prob} (1 - \prob)
&& \text{(chain rule and power rule)}\\
&= -(1 - \prob)^{-2} (-1)
&& \text{($\deriv{\prob} (1 - \prob) = -1$, as in the score exercise)}\\
&= (1 - \prob)^{-2}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting both derivatives back in:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hess_\iobs(\prob)
&= \outvar_\iobs \paren{-\prob^{-2}} - (1 - \outvar_\iobs) (1 - \prob)^{-2}
&& \text{(substitute the two derivatives)}\\
&= -\frac{\outvar_\iobs}{\sqf{\prob}} - \frac{1 - \outvar_\iobs}{\sqf{1 - \prob}}
&& \text{(write the negative powers as fractions)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
